selection: Post-hoc illustrative selections; not additional executions or a representative sample.
sanitization: Only sparse landmarks. Scenario seeds, player IDs, exact timestamps, full candidate distributions and raw event payloads omitted. Probabilities rounded to one decimal percent.
limitations: Offline outcomes describe illustrations only; no role roster or per-game label dataset is published.
Straight lines between landmarks do not reconstruct an observation trace.
All 173 observed public body reports came from impostors; general deduction is not established.
One shared frozen Phase 4 predictor; nine separately trained acting policies.

examples.title: Same suspicion, different action
examples.outcome: Full-17 votes for the impostor; full-43 explicitly skips. Reporter-pattern confound applies.

examples.title: Identification succeeds, action fails
examples.outcome: Correct first vote, then an innocent target despite a near-certain correct belief and a legal impostor target.

examples.title: Current memory loses evidence
examples.outcome: Native suspicion ties three candidates; an innocent one receives the vote. Observer never affects actions.

examples.title: Brief overconfident error
examples.outcome: No vote in the error window. This illustrative selection is not an error-rate estimate.
